standard.title: Deliver purposeful presentations
standard.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver presentations for purposes and audiences in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical, by selecting text structures, language features, literary devices and visual features, and using features of voice including volume, tone, pitch and pace
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that develop a theme or idea using precise vocabulary, pitch, tone, pace, volume and visual and digital features (AC9E6LY07). They have not yet worked at the level of selecting text structures, language features and literary devices deliberately for presentation purposes, or combining print, visual and audio elements to interpret ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations selecting structures, devices and voice features for purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Planning a presentation for purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a presentation by making deliberate choices about structure, content and mode based on purpose and audience
nodes.minimum_width: Given a presentation task, identify the purpose and audience; plan at least one structural choice and one mode choice (print, visual, audio) that serves them
nodes.typical_width: Plan a presentation by mapping purpose and audience to structural, language and mode choices — what text type, what visual and audio elements, what voice approach is appropriate and why each serves the communicative goal
wider: Prepare a presentation combining print, visual and audio elements to explore and interpret ideas, drawing on knowledge and research about perspectives different from students' own
Monitor ideas developed at each stage of creating a presentation in a blog or journal — making the planning and revision process visible

response_modes.reason: Students commonly plan presentation content without planning how structural, language, mode and voice choices will serve the audience. The decision chain — purpose → audience → structural and mode choices → voice approach — makes the planning process explicit and purposeful.

success_criteria: Identifies the purpose and audience for a presentation task
Plans at least one structural and one mode choice that serves them, with a reason

nodes.label: Voice features for audience engagement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and use voice features including volume, tone, pitch and pace to serve the purpose and engage the audience
nodes.minimum_width: In a delivery or viewing of a presentation, identify at least one voice feature (volume, tone, pitch, pace) and explain how it affects audience understanding or engagement
nodes.typical_width: Select voice features for a specific purpose and audience — explain why a slower pace suits a complex explanation, why varied pitch maintains engagement, why tone shift signals importance — and apply these choices in delivery
wider: Select features of voice for different audiences and purposes and recognise the effects these have on audience understanding and engagement — practise the same content with different voice approaches and evaluate the difference
Share feedback with a peer while planning, creating and rehearsing a presentation — develop the habit of using audience feedback to refine voice and delivery choices

response_modes.reason: Effective presentation delivery integrates content, structure, mode choices and voice features simultaneously in real time. Voice features cannot be rehearsed in isolation from content and structure — the integration is what rehearsal develops. This node is where the planned components come together in performance.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Peer feedback during rehearsal is a genuinely rich practice — it builds both the presenter's and the feedback-giver's analytical vocabulary for voice and delivery, and connects to the evaluation skills in AC9E7LY02.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one voice feature used in a presentation and explains its effect
Uses at least one deliberate voice choice in their own delivery and can explain why
